Title and Extent

THE POLICE ACT, 1888
THE POLICE ACT, 1888
ACT No. III of 1888
[For
Statement of Objects and Reasons, see Gazette of India, 1888, Pt. V, p. 130;
for Report of the Select Committee, see ibid., 1888, Pt. IV, p. 8; and for
Proceedings in Council, see ibid., 1887, Pt. VI, p. 100, and ibid., 1888, pp.
37 and 40.
This
Act has been declared to be in force in Baluchistan by the British Baluchistan
Laws Regulation, 1913 (2 of 1913).
It
has also been extended to the Leased Areas of Baluchistan, see the Leased Areas
(Laws) Order, 1950 (G.G.O. 3 of 1950); and applied in the Federated Areas of
Baluchistan, see Gazette of India, 1937, Pt. I, p. 1499.]
[17th February, 1888]
1.Title and Extent‑‑(1)
This Act may be called the Police Act, 1888.
[Sub‑section
(2) as amended by A. O., 1949, Arts. 3(2) and 4, has been subs. by the Central
Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with
effect from the 14th October, 1955).](2) It extends to the whole of
Pakistan;
[The word "and" at the
end of sub‑section (2), and sub‑section (3), were rep. by the
Repealing and Amending Act, 1914 (10 of 1914), s. 3 and Sch. II.]

Constitution of police forces for Bom. IV of 1890

THE POLICE ACT, 1888
THE POLICE ACT, 1888
ACT No. III of 1888
[For
Statement of Objects and Reasons, see Gazette of India, 1888, Pt. V, p. 130;
for Report of the Select Committee, see ibid., 1888, Pt. IV, p. 8; and for
Proceedings in Council, see ibid., 1887, Pt. VI, p. 100, and ibid., 1888, pp.
37 and 40.
This
Act has been declared to be in force in Baluchistan by the British Baluchistan
Laws Regulation, 1913 (2 of 1913).
It
has also been extended to the Leased Areas of Baluchistan, see the Leased Areas
(Laws) Order, 1950 (G.G.O. 3 of 1950); and applied in the Federated Areas of
Baluchistan, see Gazette of India, 1937, Pt. I, p. 1499.]
[17th February, 1888]
2.‑Constitution of
police forces for Bom. IV of 1890--[Subs. by A. O.,
1937, for the original section as amended by the Amending Act, 1891 (12 of
1891).] (1) Notwithstanding anything in [The
words and figures "the Madras District Police Act, 1859", omitted by
A. O., 1949, Sch.] , the Police Act, 1861, [Ins.,
ibid.] or the Bombay District Police Act, 1890, [The
words "or any Act relating to the Police in any Presidency‑town",
omitted, ibid.] the Central Government may, by notification [For such notifications, see Gen. R. & O., and the
Gazette of India, 1937, Extraordinary, dated 1st April, 1937, pp. 671 and 672,
and ibid., Pt. 1, pp. 873 and 1553.] in the official Gazette, create a
special police district embracing parts of two or more Provinces, and extend to
every part of the said district the powers and jurisdiction of members of a
police force belonging to any part of Pakistan [Subs.
by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd
Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for "the Provinces and the
Capital of the Federation" which had been subs. by A. O., 1949, Arts. 3(2)
and 4, for "British India".] specified in the notification.
(2) Subject to any orders which
the Central Government may make in this behalf, members of the said police
force shall have, within every part of any Province of which any part is
included in the said district, the powers, duties, privileges and liabilities
which, as police officers, they have in their own Province.
(3) Any member of the said police
force whom the Central Government shall generally or specially empower to act
under this sub‑section may, subject to any orders which the Central
Government may make in this behalf, exercise within any Province any part of
which is included in the said district any of the powers of the officer in
charge of a police‑station in that Province, and when so exercising any
such powers, shall, subject to any such order as aforesaid, be deemed to be an
officer in charge of a police‑station discharging the functions of such
an officer within the limits of his station.
(4) A part of a Province included
in the said district shall not by reason of that inclusion cease, for the
purposes of any enactment relating to police, to be part of that Province.

Employment of police-officers beyond the Province to which they belong

THE POLICE ACT, 1888
THE POLICE ACT, 1888
ACT No. III of 1888
[For
Statement of Objects and Reasons, see Gazette of India, 1888, Pt. V, p. 130;
for Report of the Select Committee, see ibid., 1888, Pt. IV, p. 8; and for
Proceedings in Council, see ibid., 1887, Pt. VI, p. 100, and ibid., 1888, pp.
37 and 40.
This
Act has been declared to be in force in Baluchistan by the British Baluchistan
Laws Regulation, 1913 (2 of 1913).
It
has also been extended to the Leased Areas of Baluchistan, see the Leased Areas
(Laws) Order, 1950 (G.G.O. 3 of 1950); and applied in the Federated Areas of
Baluchistan, see Gazette of India, 1937, Pt. I, p. 1499.]
[17th February, 1888]
3. Employment of
police-officers beyond the Province to which they belong. Notwithstanding
anything in any of the Acts mentioned or referred to in the last foregoing
section, but subject to any orders which the
[Subs. by A.O.,1937, for "G. G. in
C.".] Central Government may make in this behalf, a member of the [Subs. ibid., for "police‑establishment".]
police force of any [Subs. ibid., for "presidency,
province or place".] Province may discharge the functions of a
police‑officer in any part of [Subs. by the
Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch.
(with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for "the Provinces and the
Capital of the Federation" which had been subs. by A. O., 1949, Arts. 3(2)
and 4, for "British India".] Pakistan beyond the limits of the
Province and shall, while so discharging such functions, be deemed to be a
member of the police force of that part and be vested with the powers,
functions and privileges, and be subject to the liabilities, of a police‑officer
[Subs. ibid., for "that establishment".]
belonging to that police force.

Consent of Provincial Government to exercise of powers and jurisdiction

THE POLICE ACT, 1888
THE POLICE ACT, 1888
ACT No. III of 1888
[For
Statement of Objects and Reasons, see Gazette of India, 1888, Pt. V, p. 130;
for Report of the Select Committee, see ibid., 1888, Pt. IV, p. 8; and for
Proceedings in Council, see ibid., 1887, Pt. VI, p. 100, and ibid., 1888, pp.
37 and 40.
This
Act has been declared to be in force in Baluchistan by the British Baluchistan
Laws Regulation, 1913 (2 of 1913).
It
has also been extended to the Leased Areas of Baluchistan, see the Leased Areas
(Laws) Order, 1950 (G.G.O. 3 of 1950); and applied in the Federated Areas of
Baluchistan, see Gazette of India, 1937, Pt. I, p. 1499.]
[17th February, 1888]
4. Consent of Provincial
Government to exercise of powers and jurisdiction. Nothing in this Act shall be deemed to enable
the police of one Province to exercise powers and jurisdiction in any area
within another Province, not being a railway area, without the consent of the
Government of that other Province.
